claim: Breast cancer genomes contain kataegis, a novel form of mutation showers in which multiple same-strand substitutions at C:G pairs spaced one to several hundred nucleotides apart are clustered over kilobase-sized regions.
source_text: Breast cancer genomes have revealed a novel form of mutation showers (kataegis) in which multiple same-strand substitutions at C:G pairs spaced one to several hundred nucleotides apart are clustered over kilobase-sized regions
evidence_reasoning: This claim references findings from breast cancer genome sequencing studies, specifically citing Nik-Zainal et al., 2012.

claim: Kataegis is often associated with sites of DNA rearrangement.
source_text: often associated with sites of DNA rearrangement
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as a known characteristic from prior breast cancer genome studies.

claim: Kataegis can result from AID/APOBEC-catalysed cytidine deamination in the vicinity of DNA breaks.
source_text: We show kataegis can result from AID/APOBEC-catalysed cytidine deamination in the vicinity of DNA breaks
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary finding demonstrated through experimental work in the manuscript.

claim: Kataegis likely occurs through action on single-stranded DNA exposed during resection.
source_text: likely through action on single-stranded DNA exposed during resection
evidence_reasoning: This is presented as a mechanistic inference based on the experimental observations.

claim: Cancer-like kataegis can be recapitulated by expression of AID/APOBEC family deaminases in yeast.
source_text: Cancer-like kataegis can be recapitulated by expression of AID/APOBEC family deaminases in yeast
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary experimental finding demonstrated in the yeast experiments.

claim: Kataegis in yeast largely depends on uracil excision, which generates an abasic site for strand breakage.
source_text: where it largely depends on uracil excision, which generates an abasic site for strand breakage
evidence_reasoning: This is based on experimental data from UNG-deficient yeast and mechanistic inference about abasic site generation.

claim: Localized kataegis can be nucleated by an I-SceI-induced break.
source_text: Localized kataegis can also be nucleated by an I-SceI-induced break
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated experimentally using I-SceI endonuclease in yeast.

claim: APOBEC3B and 3A are the deaminases whose mutational signatures are most similar to those of breast cancer kataegic mutations.
source_text: Genome-wide patterns of APOBEC3-catalyzed deamination in yeast reveal APOBEC3B and 3A as the deaminases whose mutational signatures are most similar to those of breast cancer kataegic mutations
evidence_reasoning: This is based on comparative analysis of mutation patterns in yeast and breast cancer genomes.

claim: APOBEC3B/A are implicated in breast cancer hypermutation.
source_text: the results implicate APOBEC3B/A in breast cancer hypermutation
evidence_reasoning: This conclusion is drawn from mutational signature analysis, expression data, and functional assays.

claim: More than half of 21 sequenced breast cancers contain kataegis.
source_text: Whole genome sequencing of 21 breast cancers recently revealed the presence in more than half the cancers of a novel form of localised hypermutation (termed kataegis)
evidence_reasoning: This references data from Nik-Zainal et al., 2012.

claim: Kataegic mutations occur nearly exclusively at C residues preceded by a 5′-T.
source_text: the mutations occurred nearly exclusively at C residues preceded by a 5′-T
evidence_reasoning: This is a characteristic from the breast cancer genome sequencing study.

claim: AID/APOBEC cytidine-DNA deaminases are sensitive to the 5′-flanking sequence context.
source_text: these enzymes are sensitive to the 5′-flanking sequence context
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about AID/APOBEC enzymes, supported by citations.

claim: Members of the AID/APOBEC family deaminate cytosine in the context of a single-stranded polynucleotide substrate.
source_text: Members of the AID/APOBEC family of enzymes (reviewed in Conticello et al., 2007) deaminate cytosine in the context of a single-stranded polynucleotide substrate
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the biochemical activity of these enzymes.

claim: AID/APOBEC enzymes function in adaptive and innate immunity.
source_text: function in adaptive and innate immunity
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the physiological roles of these enzymes.

claim: AID acts on C residues in the DNA of genomic immunoglobulin loci in activated lymphocytes to trigger antibody gene diversification.
source_text: AID acts on C residues in the DNA of the genomic immunoglobulin loci in activated lymphocytes to trigger antibody gene diversification
evidence_reasoning: This is well-established knowledge about AID's physiological function.

claim: APOBEC3 family members act on C residues in the DNA of viral replication intermediates as part of a host restriction pathway.
source_text: APOBEC3 family members, of which there are seven in humans, act on C residues in the DNA of viral replication intermediates (usually in the cytoplasm) as part of a host restriction pathway
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about APOBEC3 function in antiviral immunity.

claim: There are seven APOBEC3 family members in humans.
source_text: of which there are seven in humans
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about the human APOBEC3 gene family.

claim: Off-target deamination by AID results in nucleotide substitutions and genomic rearrangements in B lymphocyte tumours.
source_text: Off-target deamination by AID results in nucleotide substitutions and genomic rearrangements in B lymphocyte tumours
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about AID's role in B cell malignancies, supported by citation.

claim: Some AID-induced mutations are implicated in oncogenesis.
source_text: some of which are implicated in oncogenesis
evidence_reasoning: This is supported by the review citation (Gazumyan et al., 2012).

claim: AID is the only member of the AID/APOBEC family known to act physiologically on endogenous nuclear DNA.
source_text: AID is the only member of the AID/APOBEC family known to act physiologically on endogenous nuclear DNA
evidence_reasoning: This is stated as established knowledge about the physiological functions of these enzymes.

claim: Other members of the AID/APOBEC family might occasionally get access to the nucleus and cause cancer-associated genomic damage or mutation.
source_text: it is possible that other members of the AID/APOBEC family might occasionally get access to the nucleus and cause cancer-associated genomic damage or mutation
evidence_reasoning: This is presented as a possibility supported by several citations suggesting this hypothesis.

claim: All tested AID/APOBEC family members expressed in yeast give a significant increase in mutation frequency.
source_text: Several members of the AID/APOBEC family members were expressed in yeast and all were found to give a significant increase in the mutation frequency
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct experimental observation from the canavanine resistance assays.

claim: The median overall intermutational distance in AID* yeast transformants is 13 kb.
source_text: the median overall intermutational distance (IMD) is 13 kb
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the genomic analysis of yeast transformants.

claim: Mutations in AID* yeast transformants are not scattered randomly over the genome but exhibit a bimodal distribution.
source_text: rather than the mutations being scattered randomly over the genome, mutation distribution is bimodal
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated through statistical analysis and comparison to Monte Carlo simulations.

claim: 52% of total mutations in AID* yeast transformants are singlet mutations with a median IMD of 156 kb.
source_text: one group exhibit a median IMD of 156 kb with a distribution of distances that is as expected for a set of individual mutations randomly scattered over the yeast genome... We designate these as singlet mutations: they account for 52% of the total mutations
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from k-means cluster analysis of the mutation data.

claim: 48% of mutations in AID* yeast transformants are proximal mutations separated by a median IMD of only 727 bp.
source_text: The remaining 48% of the mutations are much more closely spaced than would be expected on a random basis. We designate these as proximal mutations, which are separated from each other by a median IMD of only 727 bp
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from k-means cluster analysis.

claim: More than 99% of proximal mutations are within 8.5 kb of their closest neighbour.
source_text: with >99% of them being within 8.5 kb of their closest neighbour
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical result from the analysis of intermutational distances.

claim: 75% of AID*-induced proximal mutations are found in clusters of ≥5 mutations.
source_text: we find that 75% of the AID*-induced proximal mutations are actually parts of clusters
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from cluster analysis using defined criteria.

claim: Mutation clusters in AID* yeast typically extend over 6–15 kb.
source_text: These clusters typically extend over 6–15 kb (with the full range detected being 1.8–30 kb)
evidence_reasoning: This is a descriptive statistic from the cluster analysis.

claim: Mutation clusters in AID* yeast contain up to 26 mutations.
source_text: contain anything up to 26 mutations
evidence_reasoning: This is an observed maximum from the experimental data.

claim: More than one-third of AID* yeast transformants contain at least one mutation cluster.
source_text: The level of mutation clustering observed with AID* is such that more than one-third of the transformants analysed (16/40) contain at least one mutation cluster
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of 40 transformants.

claim: In affected yeast clones, a quarter to two-thirds of all mutations are concentrated in clusters that account for <0.2% of the entire genome.
source_text: In affected clones, a quarter to two-thirds of all the mutations in the cell are concentrated in a small number of clusters that account for <0.2% of the entire genome
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative analysis of mutation distribution in clustered clones.

claim: Similar mutation clusters are observed in yeast cells transformed with APOBEC3A, APOBEC3B, and APOBEC3G*.
source_text: Similar clusters were also observed in yeast cells transformed with APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B as well as with the hyperactive APOBEC3G mutant APOBEC3G*
evidence_reasoning: This is a direct experimental observation from multiple yeast transformants.

claim: Over 88% of mutations within yeast clusters are strand coordinated.
source_text: mutations within a cluster occur predominantly at either a C residue or a G residue with over 88% of mutations being strand coordinated
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from analysis of mutation strand distribution.

claim: 76% of mutations in yeast AID* transformants are C→T transitions.
source_text: the majority (76%) of the mutations in the yeast AID* transformants are C→T transitions
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from mutational spectrum analysis.

claim: Transversions are preferentially associated with kataegic stretches in yeast.
source_text: transversions do occur and these are preferentially associated with the kataegic stretches
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated through analysis of mutation types in clustered vs. unclustered regions.

claim: C→T transitions likely arise through direct replication over uracils generated by cytidine deamination.
source_text: Whereas C→T transitions will likely arise through direct replication over uracils generated by cytidine deamination
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic inference based on established knowledge of uracil processing.

claim: Transversions are due to replication over abasic sites created through uracil excision by uracil-DNA glycosylase (UNG).
source_text: transversions are presumably due to replication over abasic sites created through uracil excision by uracil-DNA glycosylase (UNG)
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic inference based on known DNA repair pathways.

claim: Transversions exhibit a 4- to 10-fold bias for C→G rather than C→A substitutions.
source_text: The transversions exhibit a strong (4- to 10-fold) bias for C→G rather than C→A substitutions
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from mutational spectrum analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: REV1 translesion polymerase inserts C opposite abasic sites.
source_text: this translesion polymerase (by virtue of its deoxycytidyl nucleotide transferase activity) inserts C opposite abasic sites
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about REV1 function, supported by citation to Nelson et al., 1996.

claim: Deficiency in either REV1 or UNG leads to a dramatic fall in the proportion of transversion mutations.
source_text: Indeed, deficiency in either REV1 or UNG led to a dramatic fall in the proportion of transversion mutations
evidence_reasoning: This is an experimental result from genetic knockout experiments shown in Table 1.

claim: UNG deficiency results in a fourfold increase in the average total mutation load in AID* transformants.
source_text: Deficiency in UNG also resulted in a fourfold increase in the average total mutation load in AID* transformants
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from comparison of wild type and ung1Δ transformants.

claim: The increased mutation load in UNG-deficient cells reflects diminished repair of AID/APOBEC-generated uracils.
source_text: This presumably reflects diminished repair of the AID/APOBEC-generated uracils
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic inference to explain the observed increase in mutations.

claim: There is an overall decrease in average total mutation load in AID* transformants of REV1 deficient yeast.
source_text: There was an overall decrease in average total mutation load in AID* transformants of REV1 deficient yeast
evidence_reasoning: This is an experimental observation from rev1Δ transformants.

claim: The decreased mutation load in REV1-deficient cells might reflect possible non-catalytic roles of REV1 during DNA damage repair.
source_text: that might reflect the possible non-catalytic roles of REV1 during DNA damage repair
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation supported by citation to Sale et al., 2012.

claim: UNG-deficiency diminishes kataegis in yeast.
source_text: Since UNG is required for the transversion mutations that are enriched in kataegic stretches, we asked whether UNG itself is required for kataegis. We found that the increased mutation load in AID* ung1Δ transformants was accompanied by a dramatic shift away from mutational clustering
evidence_reasoning: This is a primary experimental finding from analysis of ung1Δ transformants.

claim: The percentage of proximal mutations falls from 48% in wild type to 18% in ung1Δ transformants.
source_text: the percentage of mutations that are <8.5 kb from their neighbour (proximal mutations) actually 'falls' from accounting for 48% of the AID* mutations in wild type cells to 18% in ung1Δ transformants
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative comparison between wild type and ung1Δ transformants.

claim: 274 of 1064 mutations in AID* wild type transformants are found within clusters compared to 28 of 2088 mutations in AID* ung1Δ transformants.
source_text: 274 of the 1064 mutations observed in AID* wild type transformants are found within clusters compared to 28 of the 2088 mutations in the AID* ung1Δ transformants
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from cluster analysis of both genotypes.

claim: The median overall IMD increases from 13 kb in AID* wild type transformants to 41 kb in ung1Δ cells.
source_text: Thus, the median overall IMD actually 'increases' from 13 kb in AID* wild type transformants to 41 kb in the ung1Δ cells
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative comparison of intermutational distances.

claim: The average number of clustered mutations per yeast transformant is 6.9 in wild type vs 1.5 in ung1Δ transformants.
source_text: There is also an absolute fall in the amount of kataegis as judged by either the average number of clustered mutations per yeast transformant (6.9 in the wild type background vs 1.5 in the ung1Δ transformants)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative comparison of clustering between genotypes.

claim: 26 kataegic stretches were found in 40 AID* wild type transformants vs 4 kataegic stretches in 19 AID* ung1Δ transformants.
source_text: or by the frequency of kataegic events (26 kataegic stretches in 40 AID* transformants in the wild type background vs 4 kataegic stretches in 19 AID* transformants in ung1Δ background)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative comparison of kataegis frequency between genotypes.

claim: Kataegis is substantially reduced but not completely lost in the UNG-deficient background.
source_text: Thus, it is evident that kataegis is substantially reduced in the UNG-deficient background, but not completely lost
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion drawn from the quantitative analysis of ung1Δ transformants.

claim: A few residual clusters with evident strand polarity are still detected in UNG-deficient cells.
source_text: a few residual clusters (which exhibit evident strand polarity or bipolarity) are still detected
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from the analysis shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Co-expression of I-SceI with APOBEC3G* increases the likelihood of kataegis in the vicinity of the I-SceI cut site.
source_text: in the presence of APOBEC3G*, induction of a double-strand break increases the probability that mutations in its vicinity are kataegic
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated experimentally using the I-SceI system shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Induction of I-SceI expression results in an increased frequency of deaminase-dependent selectable mutation at the linked CAN1 locus.
source_text: Consistent with previous findings (Poltoratsky et al., 2010), induction of I-SceI expression resulted in an increased frequency of deaminase-dependent selectable mutation at the linked CAN1 locus
evidence_reasoning: This is an experimental observation consistent with prior work.

claim: Most breast cancers identifiable by rainfall plots as harbouring major regions of kataegis also contain clusters comprising smaller numbers of same-strand nucleotide substitutions at 5′-TC dinucleotides.
source_text: Most of the cancers identifiable by rainfall plots as harbouring major regions of kataegis also contain clusters comprising smaller numbers of same-strand nucleotide substitutions at 5′-TC dinucleotides
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from analysis of breast cancer genome data.

claim: Over 91% of kataegic C mutations in tumours PD4103a, PD4107a and PD4199a are preceded by a T.
source_text: In tumours PD4103a, PD4107a and PD4199a, over 91% of the kataegic C mutations are preceded by a T
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from sequence context analysis of breast cancer mutations.

claim: Breast cancer kataegic mutations show mild sensitivity to the identity of the base at position −2.
source_text: However, any sensitivity to the identity of the base at position −2 is exceedingly mild (average across the kataegic stretches in these three tumours is A:C:G:T = 32:20:19:29 compared to the human genome average of 30:20:20:30)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative analysis of sequence context in breast cancer kataegis.

claim: AID prefers A/G at position −1.
source_text: AID prefers A/G at −1
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about AID sequence preference from prior studies.

claim: APOBEC3G prefers C at position −1.
source_text: APOBEC3G prefers C at −1
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge about APOBEC3G sequence preference.

claim: The yeast mutation data confirm previously identified sensitivity of AID, APOBEC3C and APOBEC3G to nucleotides at positions −1 and −2.
source_text: With AID, APOBEC3C and APOBEC3G the yeast data essentially confirm the previously identified sensitivity to nucleotides located at positions −1 and −2 (AID: 5′-WRC, APOBEC3C: 5′-TYC, APOBEC3G: 5′-CCC)
evidence_reasoning: This is a confirmation of prior findings using the new yeast genome-wide data.

claim: Both APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B strongly prefer a T at position −1 (91%).
source_text: With regard to APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B, the results reveal that (consistent with earlier studies on APOBEC3B; Bishop et al., 2004), both enzymes strongly prefer a T at position −1 (91%)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from genome-wide analysis in yeast.

claim: APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B show mild discrimination with regard to bases at position −2.
source_text: the yeast studies reveal that unlike other deaminases, both APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B show mild discrimination with regard to the bases located at position −2 (APOBEC3A, A:C:G:T = 25:26:7:42; APOBEC3B, A:C:G:T = 35:14:20:31)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from sequence context analysis in yeast.

claim: APOBEC3B has a mutational signature that fits extremely well with the kataegis in PD4107a and PD4103a (p<0.005).
source_text: Comparing the contexts of the mutations obtained with the individual deaminases in yeast to those of the kataegic mutations in the cancers reveals that APOBEC3B has a signature that fits extremely well with the kataegis in PD4107a and PD4103a whereas APOBEC3A fits better with PD4199a (p values in all three cases <0.005)
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical comparison of mutational signatures between yeast and breast cancer.

claim: APOBEC3A fits better with kataegis in PD4199a (p<0.005).
source_text: APOBEC3A fits better with PD4199a (p values in all three cases <0.005)
evidence_reasoning: This is a statistical comparison of mutational signatures.

claim: A marked bias towards a 5′-T is seen amongst individual singlet C mutations in several breast tumours.
source_text: Interestingly, a marked bias towards a 5′-T is also seen amongst the individual singlet C mutations in several of the breast tumours (e.g., PD4199a, PD4005a and PD4120a
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from sequence context analysis of breast cancer mutations.

claim: APOBEC3A has been shown to be capable of causing genomic damage in mammalian cells.
source_text: Although APOBEC3A has been shown to be capable of causing genomic damage in mammalian cells
evidence_reasoning: This references prior work by Landry et al., 2011.

claim: Enforced expression of APOBEC3B leads to induction of histone γH2AX.
source_text: Enforced expression of APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B leads to induction of histone γH2AX
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated experimentally in KBM7 cells as shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Enforced expression of APOBEC3B leads to induction of 53BP1 foci.
source_text: Enforced expression of APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B leads to induction of... 53BP1 foci
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated experimentally in KBM7 cells as shown in Figure 4B.

claim: APOBEC3B is highly expressed in breast cancer cell-lines.
source_text: RNA analysis revealed that although several APOBEC3s can be expressed in individual breast cancer cell-lines, the highest and broadest pattern of expression was evident with APOBEC3B
evidence_reasoning: This is demonstrated by qRT-PCR analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Expression of APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B in some breast cancer cell-lines can be enhanced by treatment with phorbol ester or interferon alpha.
source_text: Consistent with studies in other cell-types (Madsen et al., 1999; Koning et al., 2009; Stenglein et al., 2010), the expression of APOBEC3A and APOBEC3B in some of the breast cancer cell-lines could be enhanced by treatment with phorbol ester or interferon alpha
evidence_reasoning: This is an experimental observation consistent with prior work in other cell types.

claim: Expression of AID/APOBECs cytidine deaminases in yeast generates mutations across the genome, a proportion of which are found in clusters.
source_text: Expression of AID/APOBECs cytidine deaminases in yeast generates mutations across the genome, a proportion of which are found in clusters
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary of the primary experimental findings.

claim: The stimulation of local kataegis in yeast by I-SceI break induction indicates that the process occurs during DNA break repair.
source_text: The stimulation of local kataegis in yeast by the induction of an I-SceI break indicates that the process occurs during DNA break repair
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference drawn from the I-SceI experimental results.

claim: Kataegis likely occurs by AID/APOBEC-catalysed deamination of cytidines exposed on single-stranded DNA during the resection phase of homology-mediated repair.
source_text: most likely by AID/APOBEC-catalysed deamination of cytidines exposed on single-stranded DNA during the resection phase of homology-mediated repair
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic inference based on the experimental observations.

claim: The lengths of kataegic stretches (mostly 6–15 kb) are in the same order as the extent of resection observed during yeast DNA break repair.
source_text: The lengths of the kataegic stretches (mostly in the range 6–15 kb) are in the same order as the extent of resection observed during yeast DNA break repair
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparison between observed cluster lengths and known resection lengths from the literature.

claim: The distances separating adjacent mutations within yeast kataegic stretches average about 1.2 kb in the AID* dataset.
source_text: The distances separating adjacent mutations within the yeast kataegic stretches (averaging about 1.2 kb in the AID* dataset)
evidence_reasoning: This is a quantitative result from analysis of intermutational distances within clusters.

claim: The deaminase both jumps and slides on ssDNA, acting with possibly low efficiency at each encountered cytidine.
source_text: might in part reflect that the deaminase both jumps and slides on ssDNA, acting with possibly low efficiency at each encountered cytidine as proposed by Goodman
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic inference to explain mutation spacing, supported by citation to Chelico et al., 2006.

claim: In the absence of an induced double-strand break, kataegis in AID/APOBEC-expressing yeast was greatly dependent on UNG.
source_text: In the absence of an induced double-strand break, kataegis in AID/APOBEC-expressing yeast was greatly dependent on UNG
evidence_reasoning: This is a conclusion from the ung1Δ experimental results.

claim: UNG-dependent kataegis likely reflects that kataegis was dependent on breaks generated through the processing of abasic sites.
source_text: likely reflecting that kataegis under these circumstances was dependent on breaks generated through the processing of abasic sites
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic inference to explain the UNG-dependence.

claim: Residual kataegis in the absence of UNG might reflect that breaks will occasionally occur spontaneously through other means.
source_text: That some residual kataegis is still observed in the absence of UNG might well reflect that breaks will occasionally occur spontaneously through other means
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation for the residual kataegis observed in ung1Δ cells.

claim: The finding that a double-strand break can nucleate kataegis in yeast is consistent with the close association of kataegis and rearrangements in breast cancer.
source_text: The finding that a double-strand break can be the nucleating lesion for kataegis in this yeast experimental system is consistent with the close association of kataegis and rearrangements in breast cancer
evidence_reasoning: This connects the yeast experimental findings to the breast cancer observations.

claim: APOBEC-catalysed kataegic deamination in exposed stretches of single-stranded DNA in cancer cells might itself lead to DNA breaks.
source_text: it is probable that APOBEC-catalysed kataegic deamination in exposed stretches of single-stranded DNA in the cancer cells might itself lead to DNA breaks
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative proposal about the mechanism in cancer cells.

claim: Recombinational repair of double-strand breaks in yeast is associated with an increased frequency of local mutations with implication of error-prone polymerases.
source_text: It has long been known that recombinational repair of double-strand breaks in yeast is associated with an increased frequency of local mutations with implication of error-prone polymerases
evidence_reasoning: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Strathern et al., 1995.

claim: The signatures of mutations associated with the I-SceI break implicate APOBEC3 activity rather than error-prone polymerases as the source of mutations during double-strand break repair.
source_text: In our experiments, the signatures of the mutations associated with the I-SceI break (see Figure 2D legend) implicate APOBEC3 activity rather than error-prone polymerases as the source of mutations during the double-strand break repair
evidence_reasoning: This is an inference based on the sequence context of mutations near the I-SceI site.

claim: Extensive clusters of mutations can be induced in yeast by alkylating agents acting on single-stranded DNA.
source_text: More recently Gordenin and colleagues have shown that extensive clusters of mutations can be induced in yeast by alkylating agents acting on single-stranded DNA
evidence_reasoning: This references work by Roberts et al., 2012.

claim: AID/APOBEC-mediated kataegic hypermutation can be viewed as a specialized example of localized hypermutation caused by exposure of single-stranded DNA during homologous recombination.
source_text: Thus, the AID/APOBEC-mediated kataegic hypermutation, driven by these endogenous mutagens, can be viewed as a specialised, albeit dramatic, example of localised hypermutation caused by exposure of single-stranded DNA during homologous recombination
evidence_reasoning: This is a conceptual interpretation placing the findings in a broader context.

claim: Transversions in yeast are specifically associated with kataegic stretches whereas unclustered mutations in the same cells are restricted to transitions.
source_text: It is striking that transversions in yeast are specifically associated with kataegic stretches whereas the unclustered mutations in the same cells are restricted to transitions
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from the mutational spectrum analysis.

claim: Singlet uracils largely encounter UNG as part of the base-excision repair process, which would be non-mutagenic.
source_text: we suspect the singlet uracils largely encounter UNG as part of the base-excision repair process (which would be non-mutagenic)
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation based on knowledge of DNA repair pathways.

claim: C→T transition mutations would be the result of direct replication over non-excised uracil.
source_text: the C→T transition mutations would be the result of direct replication over the non-excised uracil
evidence_reasoning: This is a mechanistic inference based on known consequences of uracil in DNA.

claim: The action of UNG on uracil in a stretch of exposed single-stranded DNA may yield an abasic site that is replicated over by a translesion polymerase rather than repaired.
source_text: In contrast, the action of UNG on uracil in a stretch of exposed single-stranded DNA may yield an abasic site that is replicated over by a translesion polymerase rather than repaired
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative mechanistic explanation for the enrichment of transversions in clusters.

claim: Other processes that cause significant exposure of single-stranded DNA could predispose to kataegis.
source_text: One can well imagine that other processes that cause significant exposure of single-stranded DNA (e.g., DNA spooling caused by replication fork stalling [Lopes et al., 2006]; R-loop structures generated during transcription of suitable target sequences [Aguilera and Gómez-González, 2008]) could predispose to kataegis
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative proposal about alternative mechanisms, supported by citations about ssDNA exposure.

claim: The cancer kataegis displays a twofold to fivefold higher average mutation density than yeast kataegis.
source_text: Comparison of the yeast and breast cancer data reveals that the kataegic stretches in both sets extend over a similar range of lengths but with the cancer kataegis displaying a twofold to fivefold higher average mutation density
evidence_reasoning: This is a comparative analysis between yeast and breast cancer kataegis.

claim: The higher mutation density in cancer kataegis could reflect differences in deaminase activity in the two organisms.
source_text: This could reflect differences in deaminase activity in the two organisms
evidence_reasoning: This is a speculative explanation for the observed difference.

claim: Cancers which harbour kataegic stretches comprising larger numbers of mutations additionally contain multiple clusters with smaller numbers of T-C mutations.
source_text: It also appears that those cancers which harbour kataegic stretches comprising larger numbers of mutations additionally contain multiple clusters with smaller numbers of T-C mutations
evidence_reasoning: This is an observation from the breast cancer genome analysis.
